newsitem.title: USA: AmEx starts Central American card product.
newsitem.headline: AmEx starts Central American card product.

text.p: American Express Co and card-issuer Credomatic said Thursday they launched the American Express card in Costa Rica, Nicaragua, Guatemala and Honduras.
The companies said the card will be launched later this year in El Salvador.
Credomatic, founded in 1970, has more than 36,000 merchants in its Central American network and more than 700,000 cards in its portfolio.
The companies said the launch followed an independent operator agreement reached in January.
Under terms of the agreement, Credomatic acquired the right to conduct the American Express Card-issuing business in five regional markets.

Credomatic is responsible for all operations supporting the American Express card, including billing and payment systems, accounting, customer servicing, credit and fraud control, and charge authorizations. Credomatic will also be responsible for marketing the card in five Central American markets.
American Express said customers in the five markets will have access to the American Express international service network and other travel and financial services.
Credomatic has also taken over responsibility for servicing local merchants accepting the American Express card in the Central American region.

American Express previously provided a U.S. dollar-denominated American Express Card to Central American customers. Existing card members in the five countries will have the option of converting their card to the new product, retaining their dollar-denominated cards, or carrying both.
A news release did not disclose any financial arrangements between American Express and Credomatic and further details were not immediately available.
